title: bug: deployment.deploy takes no per-environment schema guard, so its migration can interleave with a rollback restore or a migrate_down revert
description:
MEASURED at HEAD f6e97a6b on 2026-09-12 by architect-76be3b8c, filed as the successor that task-b8af5916c0c4476ca9f545cb2690cda0's scope fence names and that `apps/daemon/src/deployment/environment-schema-guard.ts:27` already claims exists. Raised by qa-c85c997d out of that row's QA approval: the header sentence was ahead of the board. This row makes it true.

THE HOLE THAT IS LEFT. task-b8af5916 unified ROLLBACK and MIGRATE_DOWN onto one per-environment stream, so those two now exclude each other. `deployment.deploy` was deliberately left out and still takes NO per-environment guard:

    deploy-command.ts:140   aggregateIdFor(request, null)   -- the PROJECT stream, not the environment
    deploy-command.ts:229   the same project stream, read for the stale-version check

`git grep -n environmentSchemaGuardId -- apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts` returns ZERO. A deploy that migrates can therefore be admitted against an environment while a rollback is restoring a dump over it or a migrate_down is reverting a batch. All three write the same database; all three record a receipt saying it succeeded. environment-schema-guard.ts:27-28 states this plainly and does not claim to have closed it.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE CALL SITE - MEASURED, DO NOT RE-DERIVE.

(1) DEPLOY HAS NO ADMISSION COMMIT TO RESERVE IN. `admitBootstrapCommand` (bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:278) commits nothing: it decodes, checks replay, reads the durable ledger, checks prerequisites, and returns `{handler, ledger, request}`. Deploy's ONLY durable commit is the terminal one after every effect has run - `runBootstrapCommand` -> `commitReport` -> `commitAccepted` (deploy-command.ts:137-163). Rollback and migrate_down each commit TWICE: an INTENT_PRINCIPAL decision at admission whose legs reserve the guard (rollback-command.ts:245-258; migrate-down-admission.ts:43) and a terminal that releases it. Fencing deploy means giving it an intent/reserve decision it does not have today, plus a recovery reader for that decision. `commitAcceptedLegs` (bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:228) is the multi-leg seam and already has callers in planning/, goals/ and repository/ - it is available, but it commits the TERMINAL, so it alone does not supply an admission-time reserve.

(2) IT CREATES A STRANDING MODE THE OTHER TWO DO NOT HAVE. Rollback and migrate_down deliberately leave the guard ODD when an effect's outcome is unknown, and both can still finish because recovery reads the guard id and version out of their OWN intent decision (migrate-down-admission.ts:66-70 `IntentGuard`). Deploy has no intent decision and no recovery reader, so today a crashed deploy strands nothing. Add a reserve and a daemon restart during health polling leaves that environment's schema guard odd forever - on the LONGEST-RUNNING of the three commands. The plan must answer this, not inherit it.

(3) THE PREDECESSOR'S "NO NEW VOCABULARY" RAIL DOES NOT CARRY OVER. `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:41) is a frozen four - DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT, DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING - all carrying a `DeployEngineStamp` layer. None of them means "another command holds this environment's schema", and deploy has no in-progress code at all. A NEW code is required, and it belongs at the SEAM beside DEPLOY_GOAL_UNBOUND / DEPLOY_BUILD_CONTEXT_UNCONFIGURED (thrown as `DomainRefusal` with DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM in deploy-command.ts), NOT inside the frozen engine list, which is a receipt vocabulary. This is cheap: `git grep DEPLOY_GOAL_UNBOUND` outside deploy-command.ts returns ZERO, so no closed code-to-layer map or count pin has to be reopened. Verify that grep before relying on it.

THE DECISION THIS ROW EXISTS TO MAKE - THE SPAN. This is an operator-visible availability decision, not a bug fix, which is exactly why task-b8af5916 fenced it out. `createDeployService(...).deploy(...)` (deploy-command.ts:307) spans docker build, migrate, candidate create/start and health polling under `healthBudgetMs`. Two candidate spans, and the plan must pick ONE and defend it in the module header:

    (a) WHOLE SPAN - reserve at admission, release at terminal. Strongest exclusion: nothing else touches the environment while a deploy is anywhere in flight. Cost: the environment is closed to rollback for the entire build+health window, which is the window an operator most wants to roll back IN.
    (b) MIGRATE PHASE ONLY - reserve and release around the `ports.migrate` call (deploy-command.ts:276-303). Narrow window, matches the actual schema write. Cost: the reserve/release are mid-flight commits not tied to the command's decision, and a deploy's candidate start can still interleave with a rollback restore.

Option (a) is the safer default and is what the header at :25-29 leads a reader to expect. Do NOT pick silently - confirm the span with the human at PLANNING claim, because it changes how long an environment is unavailable to other operators.

SCOPE FENCE. This row fences `deployment.deploy` onto the existing shared stream from `environmentSchemaGuardId`. It does NOT re-derive the guard, does NOT touch rollback's or migrate_down's reserve/release legs, and does NOT revisit their legacy-intent fallback. If the intent protocol turns out to need more than 8 steps, split it: the reserve/release protocol first, the arms and header second.

VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING - do not trust this description. Re-run every grep above. task-aa6f9af4735449a5b5e098f52f78fc54 is BLOCKED in the same slice and may have moved neighbouring files.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.deploy` reserves the SHARED per-environment stream before any effect runs: `deploy-command.ts` derives its guard from `environmentSchemaGuardId(projectId, environment)` and from nothing else. `git grep -n 'environmentSchemaGuardId' -- apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-command.ts` returns at least one hit, and `git grep -n 'deploy-environment:' -- apps/daemon/src ':!*.test.ts'` returns NO hit - no new private stream prefix is minted.

The SPAN is chosen and defended in writing: `environment-schema-guard.ts`'s header names exactly which deploy phases (build / migrate / candidate start / health poll) hold the guard and why, and its current :25-29 paragraph - which says deploy is NOT among the fenced commands and is only 'filed as a successor' - is rewritten to state that deploy IS fenced and over what span. The span must match what the code does, not what was hoped.

Arm: a `deployment.deploy` holding the guard makes a real `deployment.rollback` WITH restore, driven through `createRollbackCommandHandler`, refuse `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS` naming the layer that answered, AND the restore port records ZERO calls. Assert the reason code, not merely that it refused.

Mirror arm: a `deployment.migrate_down` holding the guard makes a real `deployment.deploy`, driven through `createDeployCommandHandler`, refuse with deploy's new SEAM code and its layer, AND the `ports.migrate` member records ZERO calls. `git diff` shows the new code added beside `DEPLOY_GOAL_UNBOUND` and NOT inside the frozen `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` array in `deploy-receipt-contracts.ts`.
Both new arms are proven non-vacuous: point `deploy-command.ts` back at `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` and confirm each arm goes red. Quote both reds verbatim.

The stranding question is answered with an arm, not a sentence: a deploy that leaves the guard odd (daemon restart between reserve and terminal, or a throw escaping the effect span) either recovers by reading the guard id and version out of its OWN intent decision, or is refused with a code an operator can act on. Whichever is chosen, a test drives that exact interruption and asserts the environment is not left permanently unavailable.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted. An exit code without a count line is not evidence.

If ANY of the four disagrees with what is written here, call moe.report_blocked rather than adapting - the span decision in this row's comment was derived from that exact order.

THREE SEAM FACTS THE PLAN DID NOT HAVE, each changing HOW step 3/4 must be built. None changes the SPAN (migrate-through-terminal stands); all are inside the plan's own scope fence.

D1 — A THROW FROM THE MIGRATE CLOSURE IS SWALLOWED. `migrateFor` (deploy-service.ts:150-165) wraps `ports.migrate` in try/catch and flattens a thrown value to `code@layer` string, which becomes `refuse(target, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, migrated)` at :319. So a `DomainRefusal(DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY, DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM)` thrown inside the closure reaches the operator as DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED @ DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE — precisely what DoD 4 forbids. The guard must RETURN a `DeployMigrationResult` refusal and set a seam-local flag the handler converts into the seam `DomainRefusal` (409) after `deploy()` returns.

D2 — `options.ports` REPLACES THE WHOLE PORTS OBJECT (deploy-command.ts:233 `options.ports ?? {...}`). A test that injects `ports` never composes the seam's own migrate closure, so a guard placed only inside that closure would not fence an injected-port deploy at all — and DoD 4's arm drives a REAL handler with a counted `ports.migrate` member. The guard therefore WRAPS whichever `migrate` member is in play (injected or production). This is also what makes "the `ports.migrate` member records ZERO calls" a meaningful assertion: the wrapper refuses without calling the inner member.

D3 — THE RECOVERY READER CANNOT LIVE INSIDE THE MIGRATE WRAPPER. `readReplay` (deploy-service.ts:274) returns before the migration whenever a deploy receipt for this decisionId already exists. A deploy that reserved, migrated, recorded its receipt and then died before its terminal would re-run, hit that replay, never reach the wrapper, commit a terminal with no release leg and strand the guard ODD FOREVER — DoD 6's exact hazard. The intent read runs UNCONDITIONALLY in the handler before `deploy()`.

D4 — LINE CAP. deploy-command.ts is 324 lines (cap 400, target 250). The reserve/recover/release protocol goes in a NEW leaf `deploy-schema-guard.ts`; deploy-command.ts keeps the `environmentSchemaGuardId(projectId, environment)` derivation itself (DoD 1 grep + DoD 5's mutation point both require it there).

Supporting reads, all confirmed: decisionKey = (commandId, principalId, projectId), kind-free (bootstrap-ledger.ts:68); replayOf looks up the TERMINAL key only (:258-300) so an interrupted deploy re-runs; commitAcceptedLegs (:228-249) builds legs[0] identically to commitAccepted and appends extraLegs; ExpectedVersionDecisionLeg requires legs[0] to append >=1 event and treats an exactly-empty later `events` as a read-only fence (decision-legs-contracts.ts:13-20); aggregateIdFor("deployment.deploy") = `deploy:<goalId>` or projectId (bootstrap-sequence.ts:177-181); DomainRefusal carries code/layer/detail/httpStatus (daemon-command-dispatch.ts:35-48).

READ-ONLY STEP: no files written. 16 peer/debris dirty paths in the shared checkout noted and untouched.

implementationPlan.description: ADD DEPLOY'S SEAM VOCABULARY AND ITS INTENT IDENTITY in `deploy-command.ts`, no behaviour yet. Export a new seam refusal code `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY` beside the existing `DEPLOY_BUILD_CONTEXT_UNCONFIGURED` / `DEPLOY_REQUEST_REJECTED` constants, thrown as a `DomainRefusal` at `DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` with HTTP 409 (409, not 422: it is a retryable conflict, matching what rollback answers for `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS`). DO NOT add it to `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` in `deploy-receipt-contracts.ts` - that frozen four is the ENGINE's receipt vocabulary carrying a `DeployEngineStamp`, and this refusal is minted at the seam and never reaches a receipt. Add module-private `const INTENT_KIND = "internal.deployment.deploy_requested"` and `const INTENT_PRINCIPAL = "daemon:deploy-command"`, naming the two existing precedents in a comment. Derive the intent decision key as `{ ...decisionKey(request), principalId: INTENT_PRINCIPAL }` so it is a DIFFERENT row from the terminal decision - `decisionKey` is (commandId, principalId, projectId) and does not include the kind (`bootstrap-ledger.ts`:68), which is exactly the separation rollback and migrate_down rely on.

TWO DEPARTURES FROM THE STEP TEXT, both forced by step 1's measurements, neither changing the span.

(a) THE PROTOCOL LIVES IN A NEW LEAF `deploy-schema-guard.ts`, not in deploy-command.ts. deploy-command.ts was 324 lines before this step against a 400 hard cap / 250 target; the reserve + recovery reader + release with headers is ~100 lines and would have breached it. The leaf carries `DEPLOY_SCHEMA_INTENT_KIND = "internal.deployment.deploy_requested"`, `DEPLOY_SCHEMA_INTENT_PRINCIPAL = "daemon:deploy-command"` (both precedents named in the doc comment), the two guard event types, `deployIntentRequestBytes` and `deployIntentKey`. The leaf holds NO refusal vocabulary and throws nothing — it answers with statuses/nulls and deploy-command.ts maps them onto codes, which keeps deploy's whole refusal vocabulary readable in one module and avoids a circular import. `deployIntentKey` is built as `{ ...decisionKey(request), principalId: INTENT_PRINCIPAL }` exactly as the step prescribes, through the imported `decisionKey` so the two keys cannot drift.

(b) TWO SEAM CODES, NOT ONE. `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY` (409) is the step's code, added beside DEPLOY_BUILD_CONTEXT_UNCONFIGURED / DEPLOY_REQUEST_REJECTED in deploy-command.ts and deliberately NOT in `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES`. The second, `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_INTENT_CONFLICT` (409), is what step 4's own instruction requires: it says to "assert its identity against the request bytes the way rollback-command.ts:146 and migrate-down-admission.ts:52 do", and BOTH of those precedents refuse an identity mismatch under their own distinct code (DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT, MIGRATE_DOWN_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT). The hole it closes is reachable, not hypothetical: a deploy that reserved and died before its terminal leaves no terminal decision, so `replayOf` returns null and the SAME command id resubmitted with a DIFFERENT payload re-runs the handler from the top — without this refusal it would read the earlier request's intent and release a guard it never took, freeing an environment whose schema is still mid-flight. Both codes are seam codes at DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM; the frozen engine four is untouched.

THE INTENT PREIMAGE CARRIES NO CLOCK, and that is the one subtle correctness point in this step. `bootstrapRequestBytes` folds `decidedAt` in, but an interrupted deploy re-runs and calls `clock()` again, so keying the intent's replay proof on those bytes would make every recovery look like a different request and strand the exact case the intent exists to rescue. `deployIntentRequestBytes` uses kind + commandId + correlationId + expectedVersion + principalId + projectId + the full admitted payload (which carries environment, sha and the derived goalId) and nothing else.

No test run this step: no behaviour to exercise yet. Peer dirt untouched.

implementationPlan.description: THE TAKE AND THE PUT, AS ONE CHANGE, because a reserve without its matching release is the leak epic rail 4 forbids. TAKE: inside the `migrate` port closure (`deploy-command.ts`:276-303), before `migrateWithBackup` and after `resolveDeployMigrationContext` succeeds, derive `environmentSchemaGuardId(projectId, environment)`, read `store.getAggregateVersion(guardId)`, refuse `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY` if it is ODD, and otherwise commit the intent decision via `store.commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` with the guard leg at `expectedVersion: priorGuardVersion` carrying a reserve event - storing `bytes({ guardId, guardVersion })` in `committedResultBytes` exactly as `rollback-command.ts`:248 does, so the stream actually reserved is recorded rather than re-derived later. If the admission answers `REPLAYED`, another process owns execution: refuse `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY`, do not migrate. PUT: change `commitReport` (`deploy-command.ts`:137-163) from `commitAccepted` to `commitAcceptedLegs` (`bootstrap-ledger.ts`:228), keeping LEGS[0] byte-identical to what it commits today - the project-stream leg built from `aggregateIdFor(request, null)` - and appending ONE extra leg at `{ aggregateId: guardId, expectedVersion: guardVersion, events: [release] }`. The extra leg is appended only when this deploy actually reserved; a deploy that refused before the migration (unconfigured build context, goal unbound, build failure) has no reservation and must commit with NO extra leg, which is the `commitAccepted`-shaped path today. Thread the reserved `{guardId, guardVersion}` from the closure to `commitReport` through a mutable seam-local, not through the engine or the `DeployReport` - the report is a receipt contract and must not grow a guard field.
implementationPlan.note:
THE TAKE AND THE PUT LANDED AS ONE CHANGE. tsc EXIT 0; `src/deployment` suite Test Files 27 passed (27), Tests 362 passed | 2 skipped (364), EXIT 0.

TAKE — `reserveDeploySchemaGuard` (deploy-schema-guard.ts). Reads `store.getAggregateVersion(guardId)`, refuses on ODD, otherwise commits the intent decision via `commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` with `committedResultBytes: {guardId, guardVersion}` exactly as rollback-command.ts:250 does. Answers `null` for all three failure modes (odd stream / stale leg / REPLAYED admission), and the seam maps all three to DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY. Single leg = the guard stream: deploy has no request stream of its own (its request is recorded by the terminal on the project stream), and `legs[0]` must append >=1 event, which the reserve does. NO project leg in the reserve — deliberate and documented: this reserve fires MID-FLIGHT, the project version was agreed at admission (the :229 stale check) and is agreed again by the terminal's own leg; fencing it a third time here would refuse deploys for project events that landed during a docker build.

PUT — `commitReport` now takes the reservation and branches: `commitAccepted` when null, `commitAcceptedLegs` + one release leg at `{aggregateId: guardId, expectedVersion: guardVersion}` when held. legs[0] is byte-identical either way (`commitAcceptedLegs` builds it from the same CommitPlan through the same `eventDraft`, bootstrap-ledger.ts:240-244). The release's expectedVersion is the RECORDED version, never a re-read.

THE ONE STRUCTURAL DEPARTURE, forced by step 1's D1+D2 and fully inside the span. The guard is a WRAPPER around whichever `migrate` member is composed (`guardDeployMigration`), not code inside the production closure. Two reasons, both measured: (D2) `options.ports ?? {...}` replaces the WHOLE ports object, so a composition that injects ports never builds that closure and a guard inside it would fence only the production path; (D1) `migrateFor` (deploy-service.ts:157-161) CATCHES whatever the port throws and flattens it to a DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED detail, so the refusal must be RETURNED as a `DeployMigrationResult` and the seam mints its own `DomainRefusal(DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY, DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM, 409)` after `deploy()` returns, AHEAD of `refusalOf`. Wrapping is also what makes DoD 4's "the ports.migrate member records ZERO calls" literally true: the inner port is never invoked on a busy environment.

Threading is a mutable `DeploySchemaHold {busy, reservation}` seam-local — nothing on `DeployReport`, which stays a receipt contract.

`environmentSchemaGuardId(projectId, environment)` is called IN deploy-command.ts (as `guardIdFor`), satisfying DoD 1's grep and giving DoD 5 its mutation point.

LINE CAP, managed rather than breached. deploy-command.ts peaked at 435 mid-step. I moved the wrapper body into the leaf and compressed my own comments: now 392 (cap 400), leaf 233. deploy-command.ts was already 324 before this row, so it was over the 250 target on arrival; I did not make it worse than +68 and left headroom for step 4. No pre-existing comment or code block was gutted to buy room.

implementationPlan.description: THE RECOVERY READER, which is the half that stops an interrupted deploy from stranding the environment forever. A deploy whose terminal never committed is NOT caught by `replayOf` (`bootstrap-ledger.ts`:258 looks up the TERMINAL key, finds nothing, returns null) so the same commandId re-runs the whole handler - and on the second pass the guard it reserved on the first pass is odd, so step 3's check would refuse the request its OWN earlier attempt reserved. Before the odd-parity check in the `migrate` closure, read the intent decision at the INTENT_PRINCIPAL key; when it exists, assert its identity against the request bytes the way `rollback-command.ts`:146 and `migrate-down-admission.ts`:52 do, decode `{guardId, guardVersion}` from its committed bytes, and CONTINUE on that recorded pair rather than re-deriving or re-reserving. Use the RECORDED guardId, never a fresh derivation - that is the same discipline the predecessor's legacy-intent fallback established, and it is what lets the terminal's release leg agree with a stream this request really took. Follow the predecessor on unknown outcomes and do NOT widen it: a throw escaping between the reserve and the terminal leaves the guard ODD on purpose, because the schema's state is then unknown and nothing else may move it; recovery is by re-issuing the same commandId, which this reader is what makes possible.
implementationPlan.note:
THE RECOVERY READER LANDED. tsc EXIT 0; `src/deployment` Test Files 27 passed (27), Tests 362 passed | 2 skipped (364), EXIT 0.

`openDeploySchemaHold(store, admitted.request)` reads the intent decision at the INTENT_PRINCIPAL key, asserts its identity and returns the hold pre-loaded with the recorded `{guardId, guardVersion}`; `null` means the intent on record is not this request's and the seam throws DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_INTENT_CONFLICT (409). The wrapper then skips the parity check and the reserve whenever `hold.reservation !== null`, so a re-issued command id never refuses the reservation its own earlier attempt committed.

PLACEMENT IS THE WHOLE STEP, and it is the one thing the plan's step text would have got wrong. The step says to read the intent "before the odd-parity check in the `migrate` closure". That placement STRANDS the worst case. `readReplay` (deploy-service.ts:274) returns BEFORE the migration whenever a deploy receipt for this decision id already exists — so a deploy that reserved, migrated, recorded its receipt and then died before its terminal would, on the re-issue its recovery depends on, never reach the closure at all, commit a terminal with no release leg, and leave that environment's guard ODD FOREVER. That is precisely DoD 6's "permanently unavailable". The read therefore runs in the HANDLER before `deploy()`, so the reservation reaches the terminal down every path the engine can take including the replay one. Step 6(d) drives exactly this interruption.

IDENTITY ASSERT, mirroring rollback-command.ts:64-72 and migrate-down-admission.ts:50-62: commandKind, effectDisposition, and `identifyReplayRequest(record, deployIntentRequestBytes(request)) !== record.replayRequestSha256`. Plus `guardId === intent.targetAggregateId`, which is free here because the guard stream IS the intent's primary leg. The guard id is taken from the RECORDED bytes, never re-derived — a fresh derivation would re-answer the question the record exists to answer and would strand every request that reserved before any future change to the derivation.

NO LEGACY FALLBACK, and this is a deliberate asymmetry with the other two commands rather than an omission. Rollback and migrate_down accept an intent carrying no `guardId` because theirs predate the shared stream. `deployment.deploy` was NEVER fenced before this row, so a deploy intent without a `guardId` cannot exist; accepting one would mean deriving a stream from thin air and releasing something the request never took. The roster is closed to exactly `{guardId, guardVersion}` (sorted-key compare) with the version required odd and safe-integer; anything else fails closed to CONFLICT.

THE UNKNOWN-OUTCOME WINDOW IS NOT WIDENED. A throw escaping between reserve and terminal still leaves the guard ODD on purpose — the schema's state is unknown, so nothing else may move it. What this reader buys is that re-issuing the SAME command id finishes the request and gives the environment back.

LINE CAP after this step: deploy-command.ts 398, deploy-schema-guard.ts 307 — both under the 400 hard cap, both over the 250 target. deploy-command.ts arrived at this row already 324 lines; it now has ~2 lines of headroom and the NEXT row to touch it should plan a split (same position rollback-command.ts was left in at 398). Recorded here rather than fixed in-line: extracting the production migrate-port composition would be a ~57-line move of code this row does not otherwise touch, on a shared branch with two live peer rows.

SPAN DECIDED BY THE OWNER at PLANNING claim, 2026-09-12, as this row's description required. The fork is closed — do not re-open it at implementation time.

CHOSEN: MIGRATE-THROUGH-TERMINAL. The guard is reserved inside the `migrate` port closure and released at the terminal commit.

    build -- transfer -- inspect -- env -- [RESERVE] migrate -- startCandidate -- health -- flipProxy -- [RELEASE at terminal]

WHY, and this is what the module header must say. Measured phase order is `deploy-service.ts`:279 build, :283 transfer, :287 image inspect, :297 environment resolve, :310 migrate, :322 startCandidate, :326 awaitHealthy, :330 flipProxy. Build and transfer cannot move the schema and can take minutes, and that is precisely the window an operator most wants to roll back IN — so reserving across them buys nothing and costs availability. Everything from the migration onward DOES depend on the schema holding still: a rollback restore landing while the candidate is starting or health-polling leaves the candidate serving against a schema that was restored out from under it. So the fence starts at the migration and ends with the command.

REJECTED, with reasons, so nobody re-derives them:
- WHOLE SPAN (reserve in an admission-time intent, exact structural copy of rollback-command.ts:245-258). Simplest and the best precedent match, but closes the environment across build and ssh transfer for zero schema-safety gain.
- MIGRATE PHASE ONLY (reserve and release around `migrateFor` alone). Leaves candidate start and health polling able to interleave with a restore — a real hole the header would have to admit, which is the same half-closed state this row exists to end.

THE COST THIS BUYS, STATE IT PLAINLY IN THE HEADER: the intent decision commits MID-FLIGHT rather than at admission. That is a deliberate departure from `rollback-command.ts` and `migrate-down-admission.ts`, which both reserve in an admission-time intent. Do not "fix" it back to admission — that would be re-deciding the span the owner chose.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP: the `migrate` port is a closure DEFINED AT THE SEAM (`deploy-command.ts`:276-303) and merely INVOKED by the engine at :310. It already closes over `store`, `projectId` and `clock`. So the durable reserve can fire at exactly the right point in the sequence while the commit stays in the command seam's own code — the engine never gains store-writing authority, and the seam/engine boundary this slice maintains is not crossed.

Two processes on the SAME command id both lose or one wins and the other gets REPLAYED — also null, also BUSY (deploy-schema-guard.ts:148-150). Neither loser migrates.

(2) THE RELEASE'S expectedVersion. `deploySchemaReleaseLeg` reads `reservation.guardVersion` and nothing else (deploy-schema-guard.ts:165-177). `git grep -n getAggregateVersion` across both changed production files returns exactly ONE call site, deploy-schema-guard.ts:130 — the reserve's own parity read. There is no second read anywhere, so a stream another command touched in between cannot move this leg's fence: the leg would simply fail to agree and the terminal would refuse rather than release someone else's reservation.

(3) THE RECOVERY PATH'S GUARD ID. `recordedReservation` decodes `{guardId, guardVersion}` out of `intent.resultBytes` (deploy-schema-guard.ts:283-305) and returns the RECORDED id; the derivation is never re-run there. It additionally pins `guardId === intent.targetAggregateId`, which is free because the guard stream IS the intent's primary leg. A request that reserved before any future change to `environmentSchemaGuardId` therefore still releases the stream it really took. The roster is closed to exactly `{guardId, guardVersion}` with an odd safe-integer version, and deploy has NO legacy fallback by construction — it was never fenced before this row, so a deploy intent lacking a guard id is corrupt, not old (documented at environment-schema-guard.ts's upgrade-hazard paragraph).

(4) IS THE MIGRATION GENUINELY UN-RUN ON A BUSY REFUSAL? Yes, and by structure rather than by ordering luck. `guardDeployMigration` returns the busy result BEFORE `inner(...)` (deploy-schema-guard.ts:294-299), and `inner` is the only thing that can reach `migrateWithBackup` — the seam's production closure is the inner port, and an injected one is too. The arm "a held migrate_down refuses a real deploy at the guard, BEFORE its migration port is called" asserts `migrations` is `[]` on a COUNTED port, so this is measured, not argued. Under the private-stream mutant that same arm reds with a DECIDED deploy, which is the proof the count is load-bearing.

(5) DOES THE HEADER DESCRIBE THE SPAN THE CODE IMPLEMENTS? Yes, phase by phase, at environment-schema-guard.ts:25-31: taken at the MIGRATION, given back with the TERMINAL, held across migrate / candidate start / health poll / proxy flip, NOT across docker build or ssh transfer — which matches deploy-service.ts's order (build :279, transfer :283, migrate :310, startCandidate :322, awaitHealthy :326, flipProxy :330) and the terminal at deploy-command.ts:381. The mid-flight intent is named as a deliberate departure with a DO-NOT-FIX-BACK note (:33-38). The residual is stated rather than hidden (:40-45): a rollback or revert admitted DURING the build phase is NOT excluded, takes the environment, and the deploy then refuses DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_SCHEMA_BUSY after a completed build — a wasted build, never a corrupted schema. The header explicitly does not claim the fence is total.

TWO THINGS I FOUND THAT THE FIVE QUESTIONS DID NOT ASK, both recorded rather than fixed:
  (i) The intent decision adds `internal.deployment.deploy_requested` to `readDurableLedger`'s `kinds` set and an entry for the guard stream to its `aggregates` map (bootstrap-ledger.ts:97-112). Neither can satisfy a prerequisite — `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES` names no `internal.*` kind — and `environment-schema:<64hex>` cannot collide with `projectId` or `deploy:<goalId>`, the only two ids `aggregateIdFor` mints for this command (bootstrap-sequence.ts:177-181).
  (ii) The store rejects two legs naming the same aggregate ("legs[1].aggregateId ... is fenced by an earlier leg" — seen for real in drill mutant A). That is only reachable if a project id were literally `environment-schema:<64hex>`. Not guarded against; noted so a future reader knows the constraint exists rather than discovering it from a drill.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE SIZE TRAP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS PLAN IS EIGHT STEPS RATHER THAN TWO. `environmentSchemaGuardId` is already exported, so the derivation is free - and that makes this look like a call site. It is not. Rollback and migrate_down each commit TWICE: an INTENT_PRINCIPAL decision whose legs reserve the guard, plus a terminal that releases it. Every part of the working fence hangs off that intent - the odd-parity exclusion, the recovery that finishes an already-admitted request, the legacy-id fallback. Deploy commits ONCE, at the very end: `admitBootstrapCommand` (bootstrap-services.ts:278) commits NOTHING - it decodes, checks replay, reads the ledger, checks prerequisites, returns a handler. So the real work is giving deploy a durable intent decision and a recovery reader for it; the derivation is the smallest line in the row.

WHAT THE CENSUSES BOUGHT. `internal.deployment.rollback_requested` and `internal.deployment.migrate_down_requested` appear ONLY in their own module plus environment-schema-guard.test.ts - they are internal decision-ledger kinds, absent from `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` and from every control-room roster, unlike the public `"deployment.deploy"` literal which is rostered in ~20 files. That is what keeps EPIC RAIL 1 from firing: no GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirror re-census, no `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` leg. Likewise `DEPLOY_ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS` reaches control-room only as a doc comment (live-deployments-health.ts:99) and as pass-through fixture payloads (rollback-port.test.ts:89, incident-card.test.tsx:164) - the port forwards whatever code the daemon sends, so a new seam code needs no UI change. Both facts are re-checked in step 1 rather than trusted.

WHY THE NEW CODE IS A SEAM CODE. `DEPLOY_REFUSAL_CODES` (deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:41) is a frozen four - BUILD_FAILED, DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, HEALTH_TIMEOUT, TARGET_MISSING - all carrying a `DeployEngineStamp` and all destined for a receipt. 'another command holds this environment's schema' is minted at the command seam and never reaches a receipt, so it belongs beside DEPLOY_GOAL_UNBOUND as a `DomainRefusal` at DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM. `git grep DEPLOY_GOAL_UNBOUND` outside deploy-command.ts returns ZERO, so no closed code-to-layer map is reopened.

DECISION-KEY MECHANICS THAT MAKE THE INTENT SEPARABLE. `decisionKey` is (commandId, principalId, projectId) and does NOT include the kind (bootstrap-ledger.ts:68), so an intent row under a different INTENT_PRINCIPAL is a distinct decision from the terminal - exactly what rollback and migrate_down exploit. `replayOf` looks up the TERMINAL key only, so an interrupted deploy is not replayed and the same commandId re-runs the handler: that is precisely why step 4's recovery reader is mandatory rather than defensive.
planningNotes.risks:
THE RESERVE-WITHOUT-RELEASE LEAK IS THE ONE THAT BITES, and epic rail 4 ('anything this epic starts, it stops, on EVERY exit path including the failure ones') is aimed straight at it. The migrate closure sits deep inside a try/finally in deploy-service.ts:272-330 with many `return refuse(...)` arms after the migration - candidate start failure :323, health timeout :327, proxy flip. Every one of those still reaches `commitReport`, so every one must carry the release leg. Conversely a deploy refused BEFORE the migration (build context unconfigured, goal unbound, build failed, image digest unavailable) never reserved, and firing a release leg there would commit against a stream at an even version and fail the whole terminal - turning a clean refusal into a 409 the operator cannot act on. Step 6(e) exists for exactly that arm.

THE RELEASE VERSION MUST COME FROM THE RECORD, NOT A RE-READ. If the terminal computes `expectedVersion` with a fresh `store.getAggregateVersion(guardId)` the leg will appear to work in a single-threaded test and will be wrong the moment anything else touches the stream. Use the `guardVersion` this request committed into its intent bytes, the way rollback-command.ts:248 does.

THE UNKNOWN-OUTCOME WINDOW IS DELIBERATE AND MUST NOT BE WIDENED TO MAKE A TEST EASIER. A throw escaping between reserve and terminal leaves the guard ODD on purpose - the schema's state is unknown, so nothing else may move it. The predecessor settled this and its header says so. What makes it recoverable rather than fatal is the intent reader in step 4, and deploy is the LONGEST-RUNNING of the three commands, so this is the hazard rollback and migrate_down do not have at this scale.

RESIDUAL THE HEADER MUST ADMIT: a rollback admitted during a deploy's build phase is not excluded by this fence, and will hold the environment when the deploy reaches its migration - so the deploy refuses AFTER a completed build. A wasted build, never a corrupted schema. Do not let the header imply the fence is total; that overstatement is the exact failure mode that produced this row.
